Definition: from G2596 and G3973; to settle down, i.e. (literally) to colonize, or (figuratively) to (cause to) desist:--cease, (give) rest(-rain).
BiblicalUsage: To settle down into rest is what God did on the seventh day, and what Joshua could not give, because if he had, God would not have spoken of another day. The one who has entered His rest has ceased from his own works as God did from His, and the crowd at Lystra could scarcely be restrained from sacrificing to Paul and Barnabas. Rest is the gift that stops the striving and the sacrifice both.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God's rest is still open, because Joshua's rest was only a shadow of it. I hold that ceasing from my own works is the hardest work I will ever do, and the only rest worth having.
